lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Recording Scientific Observations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about how scientists record observations.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about recording observations.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap observation diaries kept so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about how scientists record plant growth observations.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: How do scientists record observations?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.plenary: Recap facts found about recording observations.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about scientific observation at home.

lessons.title: Plant Growth Line Graph (Simple)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent plant growth data over time in a simple chart.
success_criteria: I can plot growth measurements.
I can describe the trend.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap plant measurements taken over the past two weeks.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model plotting simple growth measurements onto a chart over several weeks, discussing the growing trend.
lessons.independent_task: Children plot their plant's growth data onto a simple chart, describing what they notice.
key_questions: What do you notice about the growth?
Is it growing steadily?

differentiation.greater_depth: Describe the trend in detail and predict future growth

lessons.assessment_notes: Note data representation over time, an early introduction to line graphs — evidence for MATHS.MEA/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap the growth charts and trends.
lessons.home_link: Keep track of a plant's growth over the week.

lessons.title: Continuing to Observe Our Plants
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make detailed ongoing observations of their growing plant.
success_criteria: I can describe new changes.
I can compare to earlier observations.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the plant planted in Week 26.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model making detailed observations, comparing to earlier records.
lessons.independent_task: Children observe their plant, recording detailed changes compared to earlier entries.
key_questions: What has changed since last time?
How does it compare to your first observation?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note ongoing observational skill and comparison over time — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Check on a plant at home and note any changes.

lessons.title: Writing a Plant Growth Report
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write a short report describing plant growth over time.
success_criteria: I can describe how my plant has grown.
I can use time markers (at first, now, after two weeks).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the plant diary entries kept so far.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a short report using time markers to describe growth over time.
lessons.independent_task: Children write a short report describing their plant's growth using time markers.
key_questions: What did your plant look like at first?
What does it look like now?

differentiation.support: Complete sentence frames with time markers
differentiation.greater_depth: Write a detailed report with multiple time markers

lessons.assessment_notes: Note report writing with time sequencing, a more complex Year 2 skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Read your growth report to your family.

lessons.title: Fractions: Comparing Plant Growth
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use fraction language to compare plant growth.
success_criteria: I can say one plant grew about twice as much.
I can use fraction language to compare.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using fraction/proportion language to compare plant growth (e.g. 'this plant is about half the height of that one').
lessons.independent_task: Children use fraction language to compare their plant's growth to a partner's.
key_questions: How does your plant's height compare using a fraction?
Which grew more?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use fraction language independently and accurately

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of fractions to real comparative growth data — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Compare the size of two things at home using fraction language.

lessons.title: What If We Change the Conditions Now?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to predict what would happen if plant conditions changed.
success_criteria: I can predict a change.
I can give a reason.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap plant needs learned last week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what might happen if conditions changed now (e.g. moving a plant to a darker spot).
lessons.independent_task: Children predict what would happen to their own plant if a condition changed, with reasoning.
key_questions: What would happen if you moved your plant?
Why?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of plant needs knowledge to new predictions — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Predict what would happen if you changed a plant's location at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Growth Report Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read growth-report-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read report words.
I can read a sentence from a report.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to report-themed words (e.g. 'observe', 'measure', 'record').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
key_questions: Can you read this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading these words over the week.

lessons.title: Plant Growth Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve mixed word problems using a plant growth data context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using growth data (e.g. total growth over several weeks).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve growth-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
key_questions: How much did it grow altogether?
What is the difference between these plants?
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill applied to real class data — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a growth word problem using your plant data.

lessons.title: Plants Unit: Working Scientifically Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall the working scientifically skills used across the plants unit.
success_criteria: I can name a skill used (predicting, observing, testing).
I can give an example.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all the science skills used across the plants unit.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss the working scientifically skills used (predicting, fair testing, observing, recording, concluding).
lessons.independent_task: Children record examples of each working scientifically skill from their own plant investigation.
resources_needed: Plant investigation work from the unit
key_questions: When did you predict something?
When did you test something fairly?

differentiation.greater_depth: Give detailed examples for each skill

lessons.assessment_notes: Note metacognitive awareness of working scientifically skills, valuable for assessment across the unit — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Recap the working scientifically skills used this unit.
lessons.home_link: Explain to your family what a scientist does.

lessons.title: Presenting Our Plant Growth Journey
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present their plant's full growth journey clearly.
success_criteria: I can describe the whole journey.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap all plant diary entries and reports from the unit.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a full investigation journey.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their plant's complete growth journey to a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: How has your plant changed from start to now?
What did you learn?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific reporting progress across the whole unit — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Present your plant's growth journey to your family.

lessons.title: Shapes in Our Plants
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify shapes and symmetry in plants grown.
success_criteria: I can identify a shape in my plant.
I can say if it's symmetrical.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap shape and symmetry from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss shapes and symmetry found in the class's grown plants (leaves, flowers).
lessons.independent_task: Children examine their plant, recording shapes and symmetry observed.
key_questions: What shape is this leaf/flower?
Is it symmetrical?

differentiation.greater_depth: Identify multiple shapes and explain symmetry reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note shape/symmetry application to a natural science context — evidence for MATHS.GEO.
lessons.plenary: Recap shapes and symmetry found in plants.
lessons.home_link: Look for shapes and symmetry in plants at home.

lessons.title: Class Plants Exhibition
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to display and explain their plant investigation to visitors.
success_criteria: I can display my plant and diary.
I can explain what I did and found.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss preparing a display of plants and investigation diaries for an exhibition.
lessons.independent_task: Children set up and present their plant investigation as part of a class exhibition.
resources_needed: Plants and diaries from the unit
key_questions: What would you like visitors to know?
What are you most proud of?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note final synthesis and presentation of the whole Plants unit — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.plenary: Whole-class celebration of the plants exhibition.
lessons.home_link: Invite your family to see (or hear about) your plant exhibition.

lessons.title: Growing and Recording Plants Quiz
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about growing and recording plants.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about recording plant growth, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: Why do scientists record observations?
What can a growth chart tell us?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on this week's facts.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Charts, Fractions, Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply charting, fraction and word problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can read a growth chart.
I can compare using fractions.
I can solve a word problem.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of the week's charting, fractions, and word problems.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations covering each skill.
key_questions: What does the chart show?
What fraction is this?
How did you solve this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 28 maths observations for each child, completing the Plants unit — evidence for MATHS.STAT/N4/N2.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising fractions over the weekend.

lessons.title: Plants Unit Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise the whole Plants unit's key learning.
success_criteria: I can describe how a plant grows.
I can recall the working scientifically skills used.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap the whole three-week Plants unit.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss synthesising the whole unit's learning.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a final review and contribute to a class celebration of the Plants unit.
key_questions: What have we learned this unit?
What was most interesting?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: End of Plants unit consolidation summary for each child — evidence for SCI.PLA.
lessons.home_link: Share your favourite fact from this unit with your family.
